result.title: XposedMIA: Exploiting Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) for One-Shot Membership Inference Attacks
result.summary: Machine learning (ML) services increasingly expose explainability outputs alongside model predictions. While such explanations are intended to improve transparency, they may also reveal information about the underlying training data. In this work, we show that the local surrogate geometry employed by Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME) can be repurposed as a proxy for a sample's distance to the model's decision boundary. We extend this boundary-distance view to tabular counterfactual explanations and, for the first time, to visual counterfactual explanations for image classifiers. We present XposedMIA, a one-shot, explanation-based black-box membership inference attack (MIA) framework that converts the returned explanation into a proxy for the queried sample's distance to the model decision boundary. After a one-time calibration step on a small labeled calibration set of as few as 30 samples, our attack requires only a single query for each target sample. Unlike prior label-only attacks requiring iterative queries or shadow training, our method relies solely on the predicted label and its accompanying explanation. Our evaluation indicates that XposedMIA achieves high effectiveness, with success rates of up to 0.95 using only a single query per target, revealing that releasing explanations introduces an additional channel for membership leakage.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 XposedMIA，把 LIME 的局部代理几何以及表格、视觉反事实解释重新解读为样本到决策边界距离的代理，从而构建单次查询、无需影子训练的黑盒成员推理攻击，仅需约 30 个样本校准。
AI.relevance_reason: 「解释输出可折算为边界距离」这一思路，可能为 LVR 中的停止决策、不确定性估计或视觉反事实类证据筛选提供参照；但它属隐私安全领域，与推理状态表示的联系需核查。
